correctness.rationale: Multinomial Lucas admissibility and equality of valuations imply a unique decisive digit. Counting higher unconstrained digit triples gives Q_p=binom(p+2,3); counting decisive digits gives N_p(u), and summing levels gives S_r. The lower bound is a displacement-positive-part identity; the upper bound and unique equality follow from the exact cut-crossing formula for the permutation footrule and nonzero sum of the first (p-1)/2 residues. The standalone exact checker passed all 31,515 direct accepted-triple cases across specified finite tests, with the infinite proof supplied explicitly in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: This determines the entire distribution of a natural local statistic along adjacency edges in trinomial coefficient arrays at all prime-power sampling depths. The exceptional -1 bias changes from a maximum in the binomial case to a minimum in the ternary case; exact unique extrema for all primes p>=5 come from a sharp modular multiplication-permutation footrule. The result is mathematically motivated by the first nontrivial extension of Pascal neighbor ratios, not an arbitrary fixed modulus or routine parameter replacement.
